proposals.before: Huang led the army in person and captured Xiangping.
proposals.after: Huang campaigned against Liaodong in person and captured Xiangping.
proposals.sourceReason: Restore Liaodong, the target of the personal campaign (自征遼東).

proposals.before: Liu Cheng, whom Ren had installed at Juqiu, yielded the town, while Zhang Heng of Xinchang seized the magistrate and capitulated.
proposals.after: Liu Cheng, whom Ren had installed as magistrate of Jujiu, surrendered the town, while Zhang Heng of Xinchang seized the county head and capitulated.
proposals.sourceReason: Restore the office 令 and render 居就 as Jujiu in both English fields and repeated uses.

proposals.before: Magistrate Liu Cheng of Juqiu, whom Ren had appointed, surrendered the city; a man of Xinchang, Zhang Heng, seized the county chief and surrendered.
proposals.after: Magistrate Liu Cheng of Jujiu, whom Ren had appointed, surrendered the city; a man of Xinchang, Zhang Heng, seized the county chief and surrendered.
proposals.sourceReason: Correct the paired-field Juqiu reading; retain the existing explicit magistrate office.

proposals.before: Because Duan Liao repeatedly was a border trouble, sent general Song Hui to declare vassalage to Shi Jilong, requesting troops to strike Liao.
proposals.after: Because Duan Liao repeatedly caused trouble on the frontier, Huang sent General Song Hui to declare vassalage to Shi Jilong and request troops to attack Liao.
proposals.sourceReason: The source explicitly makes Huang (皝) the subject, but the existing literal English has no subject before sent. Restore the explicit subject while preserving the general title, repeated frontier trouble, vassalage and troop request.

proposals.before: I have dwelt in your state long; I regret not killing you.
proposals.after: I have dwelt in your state a long time and am unwilling to kill you.
proposals.sourceReason: For s0168, explicitly review the documented critical reading: Jinshu jiaozhu says the extant 恨不殺汝 is probably defective for the Tongjian’s 恨恨不欲殺汝; Yulan744 quotes 前燕錄 as 誓不殺汝. Do not treat 恨不 as simply meaning reluctant or silently emend Chinese.

proposals.before: I have lived among you too long—I should have killed you.
proposals.after: I have lived in your country for a long time, and I am loath to kill you.
proposals.sourceReason: For s0168, explicitly review the documented critical reading: Jinshu jiaozhu says the extant 恨不殺汝 is probably defective for the Tongjian’s 恨恨不欲殺汝; Yulan744 quotes 前燕錄 as 誓不殺汝. Do not treat 恨不 as simply meaning reluctant or silently emend Chinese.

proposals.before: That hope dies with me—such is fate.”
proposals.after: I never expected that this resolve would go unfulfilled; I die with lingering regret. It is fate. What can be done!”
proposals.sourceReason: Restore the unexpected failure of his resolve, his lingering regret at death and the final rhetorical question; preserve the closing quotation.

proposals.before: Troubled by Duan Liao, he sent Song Hui to submit to Shi Hu and beg for an allied expedition.
proposals.after: Because Duan Liao repeatedly troubled his borders, Huang sent General Song Hui to Shi Hu to declare Huang’s vassalage and request troops to attack Duan Liao.
proposals.sourceReason: Restore repeated border trouble, the general title and the specific request for troops; name Huang explicitly to avoid attributing his vassalage to the envoy.

proposals.before: After a fortnight’s siege his officers begged him to yield.
proposals.after: After the two sides held each other off for more than ten days, his attendants urged Huang to surrender.
proposals.sourceReason: Render 旬餘 as more than ten days, 左右 as attendants, and make Huang the explicit recipient of their advice.

proposals.before: And now the Empress Dowager, overcome with indignation, has suddenly passed away.
proposals.after: Matters came to the point that the Empress Dowager, overcome with indignation, suddenly passed away.
proposals.sourceReason: Proposed retrospective rendering of the outcome of the Su Jun/Zu Yue crisis; avoid presenting the dowager’s death as a fresh event during this later memorial. Independently check the interpretation of 至今 against the complete memorial and dated source witness before approval.

proposals.before: Until now the Empress Dowager gave vent to her indignation and in one morning ascended to distant heaven.
proposals.after: It came to this: the Empress Dowager gave vent to her indignation and in one morning ascended to distant heaven.
proposals.sourceReason: Proposed retrospective rendering of the outcome of the Su Jun/Zu Yue crisis; avoid presenting the dowager’s death as a fresh event during this later memorial. Independently check the interpretation of 至今 against the complete memorial and dated source witness before approval.

proposals.before: After Duan Liao’s fall Murong Han fled to Yuwen Gui, reckoned his fame would never let him live, and feigned madness—drinking, singing, and disheveled hair.
proposals.after: After Duan Liao’s defeat, Murong Han, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Yuwen Gui. Believing that his long-established fame and prestige would ultimately endanger his life, he feigned madness, drinking without restraint, letting his hair hang loose, and singing and shouting.
proposals.sourceReason: Restore the omitted 建威 title and the long-established fame and prestige; preserve the complete account of feigned madness.

proposals.before: In the beginning, when Duan Liao was defeated, Jianwei Han fled to Yuwen Gui; himself thought his awe-inspiring name long had shaken others, in the end could not preserve whole; thereupon feigned madness, wantonly drank, let hair down and sang and shouted.
proposals.after: Earlier, when Duan Liao was defeated, Han, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Yuwen Gui. He thought that, because his fame and prestige had long been renowned, he would not ultimately be able to remain safe; so he feigned madness, drank without restraint, let his hair hang loose, and sang and shouted.
proposals.sourceReason: Translate 建威 as an office, rather than leaving Jianwei as an apparent personal name; retain all paired-field propositions.

proposals.before: Huang sent the trader Wang Che to spy; Murong Han met him in silence, only clutching his chest.
proposals.after: Huang secretly sent the merchant Wang Che to observe Han; when Han saw Che he said nothing and only stroked his chest.
proposals.sourceReason: Restore 陰 and the explicit observation target; render 撫膺 without changing it to clutching.

proposals.before: He enfeoffed more than a hundred deserving officers.
proposals.after: More than a hundred deserving officers were enfeoffed.
proposals.sourceReason: Proposed passive rendering preserves the unexpressed Chinese subject without silently choosing Huang as grantor. This does not resolve the held extraction event attribution.

proposals.before: Enfeoffed the various meritorious ministers over a hundred persons.
proposals.after: More than a hundred meritorious officials were enfeoffed.
proposals.sourceReason: Preserve the enfeoffment and number without supplying an unexpressed grantor; independently review in the complete imperial-grant context.

extractionProposals.sourceReason: Apply the same source-backed place reading to the title alias; retain alias kind, Chinese witness and person assignment.
Apply the same place reading to the repeated event description; all dateContext and other claim fields remain unchanged.
Carry the source-backed office translation into the active title alias, retaining the title kind, Chinese witness, evidence and person assignment.

units.zh: 皝自征遼東，克襄平。
units.literal: Huang personally campaigned Liaodong, took Xiangping.
units.en: Huang led the army in person and captured Xiangping.

units.zh: 仁所署居就令劉程以城降，新昌人張衡執縣宰以降。
units.literal: Magistrate Liu Cheng of Juqiu, whom Ren had appointed, surrendered the city; a man of Xinchang, Zhang Heng, seized the county chief and surrendered.
units.en: Liu Cheng, whom Ren had installed at Juqiu, yielded the town, while Zhang Heng of Xinchang seized the magistrate and capitulated.

units.zh: 於是斬仁所置守宰，分徙遼東大姓於棘城，置和陽、武次、西樂三縣而歸。
units.literal: Thereupon he executed the guardians and magistrates Ren had installed, moved the great clans of Liaodong in groups to Jicheng, established the three counties of Heyang, Wuci, and Xile, and returned.
units.en: He executed Ren’s officials, relocated the leading Liaodong families to Jicheng, established the three counties of Heyang, Wuci, and Xile, and marched home.

units.zh: 皝以段遼屢為邊患，遣將軍宋回稱籓于石季龍，請師討遼。
units.literal: Because Duan Liao repeatedly was a border trouble, sent general Song Hui to declare vassalage to Shi Jilong, requesting troops to strike Liao.
units.en: Troubled by Duan Liao, he sent Song Hui to submit to Shi Hu and beg for an allied expedition.

units.zh: 季龍於是總眾而至。
units.literal: Jilong thereupon assembled host and arrived.
units.en: Shi Hu thereupon marched his whole host to join the war.

units.zh: 皝率諸軍攻遼令支以北諸城，遼遣其將段蘭來距，大戰，敗之，斬級數千，掠五千餘戶而歸。
units.literal: Huang led the various armies to attack Liao’s cities north of Lingzhi; Liao sent his general Duan Lan to resist; great battle, defeated them, took several thousand heads, plundered over five thousand households and returned.
units.en: Huang stormed Duan Liao’s strongholds north of Lingzhi, crushed Duan Lan, took thousands of heads, and carried off more than five thousand households.

units.zh: 季龍至徐無，遼奔密雲山。
units.literal: Jilong reached Xuwu; Liao fled to Miyun Mountain.
units.en: Shi Hu reached Xuwu while Duan Liao fled into Miyun Mountain.

units.zh: 季龍進入令支，怒皝之不會師也，進軍擊之，至於棘城，戎卒數十萬，四面進攻，郡縣諸部叛應季龍者三十六城。
units.literal: Jilong entered Lingzhi, angry that Huang had not joined forces, advanced army to strike him, reaching Jicheng; Rong soldiers several hundred thousand, four sides advanced attack; prefectures and counties various divisions rebelled responding to Jilong thirty-six cities.
units.en: Shi Hu entered Lingzhi, furious that Huang had not joined forces, advanced to strike him as far as Jicheng; several hundred thousand troops attacked from all four sides, and thirty-six cities among the prefectures, counties, and various divisions rebelled in response to Shi Hu.

units.zh: 相持旬餘，左右勸皝降。
units.literal: Stood off over ten days; left and right urged Huang to surrender.
units.en: After a fortnight’s siege his officers begged him to yield.

units.zh: 皝曰：「孤方取天下，何乃降人乎！」
units.literal: Huang said: “I am about to take All under Heaven—how then become another’s surrendered man!”
units.en: Huang snapped, “I mean to seize the realm—why would I surrender?”

units.zh: 遣子恪等率騎二千，晨出擊之。
units.literal: Sent his son Ke and others leading two thousand cavalry; at dawn they sortied and struck them.
units.en: He sent his son Ke and others with two thousand horse in a dawn sally.

units.zh: 季龍諸軍驚擾，棄甲而遁。
units.literal: Jilong’s various armies were alarmed and disturbed, cast armor and fled.
units.en: Shi Hu’s host panicked and bolted, leaving their armor.

units.zh: 恪乘勝追之，斬獲三萬餘級，築戍凡城而還。
units.literal: Ke, riding the victory, pursued them, beheaded and captured over thirty thousand heads, built a garrison at Fancheng and returned.
units.en: Murong Ke pressed the victory in pursuit, killed or captured over thirty thousand, built a garrison at Fancheng, and returned.

units.zh: 段遼遣使詐降于季龍，請兵應接。
units.literal: Duan Liao sent envoys feigning surrender to Jilong, requesting troops to meet and escort.
units.en: Duan Liao feigned submission to Shi Hu and asked for an escort.

units.zh: 季龍遣其將麻秋率眾迎遼，恪伏精騎七千於密雲山，大敗之，獲其司馬陽裕、將軍鮮于亮，擁段遼及其部眾以歸。
units.literal: Jilong sent his general Ma Qiu leading a host to meet Liao; Ke stationed seven thousand picked cavalry in ambush at Miyun Mountain and greatly defeated them, captured their marshal Yang Yu and general Xianyu Liang, and brought Duan Liao and his followers back.
units.en: Shi Hu sent his general Ma Qiu with troops to meet Duan Liao. Murong Ke stationed seven thousand elite cavalry in ambush at Miyun Mountain and routed them, captured marshal Yang Yu and general Xianyu Liang, and brought Duan Liao and his followers back.

units.zh: 若親黨后族，必有傾辱之禍。
units.literal: If they favored kin and the empress's clan, disaster of overthrow and humiliation was sure to follow.
units.en: when they favored kin and the empress's clan, overthrow and humiliation were sure to follow.

units.zh: 是以周之申伯號稱賢舅，以其身籓於外，不握朝權。
units.literal: Therefore Shen Bo of Zhou was called the worthy maternal uncle, because he was enfeoffed outside as a frontier lord and did not hold court power.
units.en: Shen Bo of Zhou was praised as a worthy maternal uncle because he held a frontier fief and did not grasp court power.

units.zh: 降及秦昭，足為令主，委信二舅，幾至亂國。
units.literal: Descending to King Zhao of Qin, who was enough to be called a fine ruler, he entrusted his two maternal uncles and nearly brought the state to disorder.
units.en: Even King Zhao of Qin, a capable ruler, trusted his two maternal uncles and nearly ruined the state.

units.zh: 逮于漢武，推重田蚡，萬機之要，無不決之。
units.literal: Reaching Emperor Wu of Han, who elevated Tian Fen, none of the myriad affairs' essentials went undecided by him.
units.en: Emperor Wu of Han elevated Tian Fen until every vital decision passed through him.

units.zh: 及蚡死後，切齒追恨。
units.literal: After Fen died, the emperor gnashed his teeth in later regret.
units.en: After Fen died, the emperor gnashed his teeth in bitter regret.

units.zh: 成帝暗弱，不能自立，內惑豔妻，外恣五舅，卒令王莽坐取帝位。
units.literal: Emperor Cheng was dim and weak, unable to stand on his own; inwardly confused by a beautiful wife, outwardly indulging the five maternal uncles, he finally let Wang Mang take the imperial throne without effort.
units.en: Emperor Cheng was weak and could not stand alone; beguiled within by a beautiful consort and indulging the five maternal uncles without, he finally let Wang Mang seize the throne without effort.

units.zh: 每覽斯事，孰不痛惋！
units.literal: Each time one reads these affairs, who does not feel pain and regret!
units.en: Reading such cases, who does not feel pain and regret!

units.zh: 設使舅氏賢若穰侯、王鳳，則但聞有二臣，不聞有二主。
units.literal: Suppose the maternal uncles were worthy like the Marquis of Rang and Wang Feng, then one would only hear of two ministers, not two lords.
units.en: If maternal uncles were worthy like the Marquis of Rang or Wang Feng, one would hear of two ministers, not two rulers.

units.zh: 若其不才，則有竇憲、梁冀之禍。
units.literal: If they lacked talent, there were the disasters of Dou Xian and Liang Ji.
units.en: If they lacked talent, disasters like those of Dou Xian and Liang Ji followed.

units.zh: 凡此成敗，亦既然矣。
units.literal: All these successes and failures are already thus clear.
units.en: The lesson of these successes and failures is already plain.

units.zh: 苟能易軌，可無覆墜。
units.literal: If one could change course, one could avoid overturn and collapse.
units.en: If one could change course, overturn and collapse can be avoided.

units.zh: 陛下命世天挺，當隆晉道，而遭國多難，殷憂備嬰，追述往事，至今楚灼。
units.literal: Your Majesty is heaven-born to the age, destined to exalt Jin's Way, yet has encountered many hardships of state; deep grief presses on every side; recalling past affairs, to this day one burns with anguish.
units.en: Your Majesty is heaven-born to the age, destined to exalt Jin's Way, yet has encountered many hardships of state; deep grief presses on every side, and recalling past affairs still burns with anguish to this day.

units.zh: 跡其所由，實因故司空亮居元舅之尊，勢業之重，執政裁下，輕侮邊將，故令蘇峻、祖約不勝其忿，遂致敗國。
units.literal: Tracing where it came from, it was truly because the late Minister of Works Yu Liang occupied the honor of chief maternal uncle and the weight of power and achievement, governed and judged subordinates, and lightly insulted frontier generals, so that Su Jun and Zu Yue could not contain their rage and thus brought disaster on the state.
units.en: Tracing where it came from, it was truly because the late Minister of Works Yu Liang occupied the honor of chief maternal uncle and the weight of power and achievement, governed and judged subordinates, and lightly insulted frontier generals, so that Su Jun and Zu Yue could not contain their rage and thus brought disaster on the state.

units.zh: 至今太后發憤，一旦升遐。
units.literal: Until now the Empress Dowager gave vent to her indignation and in one morning ascended to distant heaven.
units.en: And now the Empress Dowager, overcome with indignation, has suddenly passed away.

units.zh: 若社稷不靈，人神無助，豺狼之心當可極邪！
units.literal: If the altars were not numinous and men and spirits gave no aid, would the heart of wolves and jackals be allowed to reach its limit!
units.en: Had the altars not been numinous and men and spirits not aided us, would the hearts of wolves and jackals have been allowed to run their course!

units.zh: 前事不忘，後事之表，而中書監、左將軍冰等內執樞機，外擁上將，昆弟並列，人臣莫疇。
units.literal: Past events, if not forgotten, are a model for later affairs; yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows grasp the pivot within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side, with no other minister to match them.
units.en: Past events, if not forgotten, are a model for later affairs; yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows grasp the pivot within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side, with no other minister to match them.

units.zh: 陛下深敦渭陽，冰等自宜引領。
units.literal: Your Majesty deeply honors the ties of Weiyang; Bing and the others ought themselves to stretch their necks in expectation.
units.en: Your Majesty deeply honors the ties of Weiyang; Bing and his fellows ought themselves to stretch their necks in expectation.

units.zh: 臣常謂世主若欲崇顯舅氏，何不封以籓國，豐其祿賜，限其勢利，使上無偏優，下無私論。
units.literal: Your servant often says: if a ruler of the age wishes to honor the maternal clan, why not enfeoff them with vassal states, enrich their stipends and gifts, and limit their power and advantage, so that above there is no partial favor and below no private talk.
units.en: Your servant often says: if a ruler of the age wishes to honor the maternal clan, why not enfeoff them with vassal states, enrich their stipends and gifts, and limit their power and advantage, so that above there is no partial favor and below no private talk.

units.zh: 如此，榮辱何從而生！
units.literal: Thus, from what would honor and disgrace arise!
units.en: Then whence would honor or disgrace arise!

units.zh: 噂𠴲何辭而起！
units.literal: From what words would slander and calumny spring!
units.en: Whence would slander spring!

units.zh: 往者惟亮一人，宿有名望，尚致世變，況今居之者素無聞焉！
units.literal: Formerly there was only Yu Liang alone, long with a name of standing, yet still he brought change to the age; how much more those who hold the posts today, who from the first had no renown!
units.en: Formerly Yu Liang alone, though long renowned, still brought turmoil; how much more those who hold power today and were never heard of before!

units.zh: 且人情易惑，難以戶告，縱今陛下無私于彼，天下之人誰謂不私乎！
units.literal: Moreover human feelings are easily confused and hard to tell door to door; even if Your Majesty today has no partiality toward them, who in the realm would say there is none!
units.en: Human feelings are easily swayed and cannot be told house to house; even if Your Majesty is impartial, who in the realm will believe it!

units.zh: 臣與冰等名位殊班，出處懸邈，又國之戚昵，理應降悅，以適事會。
units.literal: Your servant and Bing and the others differ in rank and status and are far apart in our situations; moreover, they are close kin of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.
units.en: Your servant and Bing and the others differ in rank and status and are far apart in our situations; moreover, they are close kin of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.

units.zh: 臣獨矯抗此言者，上為陛下，退為冰計，疾苟容之臣，坐鑒得失。
units.literal: Your servant alone presses this contrary speech: for Your Majesty above, for Bing's sake below; despising ministers who only accommodate; sitting in judgment of gain and loss.
units.en: I speak against the tide alone: for Your Majesty above and for Bing's sake below, hating ministers who only flatter and judging gain and loss plainly.

units.zh: 顛而不扶，焉用彼相！
units.literal: If one does not right what is overturned, what use is that minister!
units.en: If one does not right what is overturned, of what use is that minister!

units.zh: 昔徐福陳霍氏之戒，宣帝不從，至令忠臣更為逆族，良由察之不審，防之無漸。
units.literal: Formerly Xu Fu set forth the warning of the Huo clan; Emperor Xuan did not follow it, so that even loyal ministers became a rebellious lineage, truly because investigation was not careful and precautions were not taken at the first signs.
units.en: Formerly Xu Fu warned against the Huo clan; Emperor Xuan did not heed him, and loyal ministers became a traitorous house because he did not examine carefully or guard against gradual encroachment.

units.zh: 臣今所陳，可謂防漸矣。
units.literal: What your servant now sets forth may be called prevention at the first sign.
units.en: What I now set forth is prevention at the first sign.

units.zh: 但恐陛下不明臣之忠，不用臣之計，事過之日，更處焦爛之後耳。
units.literal: Only fearing that Your Majesty may not understand your servant's loyalty and may not use your servant's plan; after the affair has passed, one will again be in the charred wreckage.
units.en: I fear only that Your Majesty may not see my loyalty or use my plan, and that after disaster passes you will again stand amid the ashes.

units.zh: 昔王章、劉向每上封事，未嘗不指斥王氏，故令二子或死或刑。
units.literal: Formerly Wang Zhang and Liu Xiang, each time they submitted sealed memorials, never failed to denounce the Wang clan, so both men ended dead or under punishment.
units.en: Formerly Wang Zhang and Liu Xiang denounced the Wang clan in every sealed memorial and ended dead or punished.

units.zh: 谷永、張禹依違不對，故容身苟免，取譏於世。
units.literal: Gu Yong and Zhang Yu equivocated and did not answer directly, so they preserved themselves and escaped, drawing ridicule from the age.
units.en: Gu Yong and Zhang Yu equivocated and preserved themselves, winning only the age's ridicule.

units.zh: 臣被髮殊俗，位為上將，夙夜惟憂，罔知所報，惟當外殄寇仇，內盡忠規，陳力輸誠，以答國恩。
units.literal: Your servant wears his hair loose and follows different customs, holds the rank of supreme general, worries day and night and knows not how to repay, and can only destroy enemies abroad, exhaust loyal remonstrance within, exert strength and offer sincerity to answer the state's grace.
units.en: I wear my hair loose and follow different customs, hold the rank of supreme general, worry day and night and know not how to repay, and can only destroy enemies abroad, exhaust loyal remonstrance within, and exert strength and offer sincerity to answer the state's grace.

units.zh: 臣若不言，誰當言者！
units.literal: If your servant does not speak, who will speak!
units.en: If I do not speak, who will!

units.zh: 初，段遼之敗也，建威翰奔于宇文歸，自以威名夙振，終不保全，乃陽狂恣酒，被髮歌呼。
units.literal: In the beginning, when Duan Liao was defeated, Jianwei Han fled to Yuwen Gui; himself thought his awe-inspiring name long had shaken others, in the end could not preserve whole; thereupon feigned madness, wantonly drank, let hair down and sang and shouted.
units.en: After Duan Liao’s fall Murong Han fled to Yuwen Gui, reckoned his fame would never let him live, and feigned madness—drinking, singing, and disheveled hair.

units.zh: 歸信而不禁，故得周遊自任，至於山川形便，攻戰要路，莫不練之。
units.literal: Gui believed and did not restrain; therefore was able to roam at will, reaching mountains and rivers’ forms and conveniences, attack and battle crucial roads—none not practiced.
units.en: Yuwen Gui believed the act and did not restrain him, so Han could roam at will and became thoroughly familiar with the terrain and the key routes for attack and battle.

units.zh: 皝遣商人王車陰使察翰，翰見車無言，撫膺而已。
units.literal: Huang sent merchant Wang Che secretly to observe Han; Han seeing Che spoke nothing, stroked his breast only.
units.en: Huang sent the trader Wang Che to spy; Murong Han met him in silence, only clutching his chest.

units.zh: 車還以白，皝曰：「翰欲來也。」
units.literal: Che returned and reported; Huang said: “Han wishes to come.”
units.en: Wang Che reported the sign; Huang said, “He wants to come home.”

units.zh: 乃遣車遺翰弓矢，翰乃竊歸駿馬，攜其二子而還。
units.literal: Thereupon sent Che to present Han bow and arrows; Han then stole fine horses, carried his two sons and returned.
units.en: He sent Wang Che with a bow and arrows; Murong Han stole horses and rode back with his two sons.

units.zh: 使陽裕、唐柱等築龍城，構宮廟，改柳城為龍城縣。
units.literal: Had Yang Yu, Tang Zhu, and others build Longcheng, construct palace and temples, changed Liucheng to Longcheng county.
units.en: He had Yang Yu and Tang Zhu build Longcheng, raised palaces and shrines, and renamed Liucheng county Longcheng.

units.zh: 於是成帝使兼大鴻臚郭希持節拜皝侍中、大都督河北諸軍事、大將軍、燕王，其餘官皆如故。
units.literal: Thereupon Emperor Cheng sent concurrent Grand Herald Guo Xi bearing credentials to appoint Huang Palace Attendant, Grand Commander of all military affairs north of the Yellow River, Grand General, King of Yan; the rest of offices all as before.
units.en: Emperor Cheng then sent concurrent Grand Herald Guo Xi bearing credentials to appoint Huang Palace Attendant, Grand Commander of all military affairs north of the Yellow River, Grand General, and King of Yan, leaving the rest of his offices as before.

units.zh: 封諸功臣百餘人，
units.literal: Enfeoffed the various meritorious ministers over a hundred persons.
units.en: He enfeoffed more than a hundred deserving officers.

units.zh: 及遼奔走，翰又北投宇文歸。
units.literal: When Liao fled in defeat, Han again north threw himself to Yuwen Gui.
units.en: When Duan Liao fled in defeat, Han again went north to Yuwen Gui.

units.zh: 既而逃，歸乃遣勁騎百餘追之。
units.literal: Having then fled, Gui thereupon sent fierce cavalry over a hundred to pursue him.
units.en: Han then fled, and Gui sent over a hundred picked cavalry to pursue him.

units.zh: 翰遙謂追者曰：「吾既思戀而歸，理無反面。
units.literal: Han from afar told the pursuers: “I already long to return; in principle there is no turning back.
units.en: He shouted to them, “I mean to go home—I will not turn back.

units.zh: 吾之弓矢，汝曹足知，無為相逼，自取死也。
units.literal: My bow and arrows you lot fully know; do not press me and seek your own deaths.
units.en: You know my bow and arrows well enough—do not press me and bring death on yourselves.

units.zh: 吾處汝國久，恨不殺汝。
units.literal: I have dwelt in your state long; I regret not killing you.
units.en: I have lived among you too long—I should have killed you.

units.zh: 汝可百步豎刀，吾射中者，汝便宜反；
units.literal: You can at a hundred paces set up a blade; if my shot hits, you then should turn back;
units.en: Plant a blade at a hundred paces—if I hit it, withdraw;

units.zh: 不中者，可來前也。」
units.literal: if not center, you may come forward.”
units.en: if I miss, come on.”

units.zh: 歸騎解刀豎之，翰一發便中刀鐶，追騎乃散。
units.literal: Gui’s riders undid a blade and set it up; Han one shot then hit the blade ring; pursuing riders then scattered.
units.en: They fixed a blade; his first arrow struck the ring and they broke off the chase.

units.zh: 既至，皝甚加恩禮，
units.literal: Having arrived, Huang greatly added favor and ceremony.
units.en: Huang welcomed him with rich honors.

units.zh: 建元二年，從皝討宇文歸，臨陣為流矢所中，臥病積時。
units.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, he followed Huang to campaign against Yuwen Gui; on the line of battle he was struck by a stray arrow; he lay ill a long time.
units.en: In the second year of Jianyuan, he joined the war on Yuwen Gui, took a stray shaft, and lay long ill.

units.zh: 後疾漸愈，於其家中騎馬自試，或有人告翰私習騎，疑為非常。
units.literal: Later illness gradually improved; at his home mounted horse to test himself; someone reported Han privately practiced riding, suspected as unusual.
units.en: Later, as his illness gradually improved, he tried riding at home to test himself; someone reported that Han was privately practising riding and suspected something extraordinary.

units.zh: 皝素忌之，遂賜死焉。
units.literal: Huang had long been jealous of him; thereupon granted him death.
units.en: Huang, who had long been jealous of him, thereupon granted him death.

units.zh: 翰臨死謂使者曰：「翰懷疑外奔，罪不容誅，不能以骸骨委賊庭，故歸罪有司。
units.literal: Han nearing death told the envoy: “Han harbored suspicion and fled abroad; the crime is too great for death to atone; I could not cast my bones in the bandit court; therefore I returned to submit to the responsible officials.
units.en: Nearing death Murong Han told the envoy, “Han harbored distrust and fled abroad; my crime is too great for death to atone; I could not leave my bones in a rebel court, so I returned to submit to the authorities.

units.zh: 天慈曲湣，不肆之市朝，今日之死，翰之生也。
units.literal: Heaven’s kindness bent pity, did not display me in the marketplace; today’s death is Han’s life.
units.en: The king spared me a public execution—this death is mercy.

units.zh: 但逆胡跨據神州，中原未靖，翰常克心自誓，志吞醜虜，上成先王遺旨，下謝山海之責。
units.literal: But the rebellious Hu occupy the Divine Land, and the Central Plain is not yet pacified; Han has always steeled his heart and sworn an oath, intent on swallowing up the vile enemies, above to fulfil the late king's last instructions and below to discharge his duty to the land of mountains and seas.
units.en: But the rebel Hu barbarians straddle and hold the Divine Land, and the Central Plain is not yet pacified. I always steeled my heart and swore that I would swallow up the vile caitiffs, above to fulfil the late king's dying wish and below to discharge my duty to the realm between the mountains and the sea.

units.zh: 不圖此心不遂，沒有餘恨，命也奈何！」
units.literal: Did not expect this heart not to succeed; dying there is surplus regret—fate it—what to do!”
units.en: That hope dies with me—such is fate.”

units.zh: 仰藥而死。
units.literal: Raised poison and died.
units.en: He drank the poison and died.

references.quote: 仁所署居就令劉程以城降，新昌人張衡執縣宰以降。
皝以段遼屢為邊患，遣將軍宋回稱籓于石季龍，請師討遼。
初，段遼之敗也，建威翰奔于宇文歸，自以威名夙振，終不保全，乃陽狂恣酒，被髮歌呼。
皝遣商人王車陰使察翰，翰見車無言，撫膺而已。
不圖此心不遂，沒有餘恨，命也奈何！」
至今太后發憤，一旦升遐。

references.title: 晉書斠注 七十一v109–110
references.quote: 《晉書》校文五曰《御覽》七百四十四引前燕錄作誓不殺汝詳語意崔錄似得其眞又攷《通鑑》作恨恨不欲殺汝注恨恨相戀之情與誓字語意正合此語温公必有所本疑恨不殺汝四字卽恨恨不欲殺汝一語之譌脫
